overallAssessment.narrative: Reg Sackey-Addo is a product engineer whose career matches what this role actually rewards: turning ambiguous customer needs into working production software across React/TypeScript frontends, relational data (Supabase/Postgres), and third-party systems. At CModel he owned AI features, integrations, and cross-system workflows from product definition through production, and helped migrate the product from Bubble prototypes to a conventional TypeScript stack. His integrations and production-debugging record is the strongest part of the case; the one material gap is no direct education-domain experience, though nothing in his record suggests difficulty transferring into a new product domain.

themes.title: Own features end-to-end from ambiguous customer needs to production delivery
themes.narrative: Reg repeatedly does the hard part of this job: taking poorly specified needs to shipped features. At CModel he owned an email-to-decision-intelligence workflow from product definition through production and built the strategic assistant as a standalone Next.js/TypeScript application, including validation and failure handling for non-conforming model output. He also built Reaccord, an independent consumer behavior-change product, end to end — architecture, interaction model, onboarding, and daily-use workflows — which is direct evidence of rapid iteration on a consumer-facing product with real ownership of what gets built, not just how.

themes.title: Model application data using relational databases
themes.narrative: Reg models application data with the whole system in mind. At Reaccord he designed a persistence layer that keeps durable relationships (goals → plans → actions → completion → reflection) while validating application-consumed state against shared Zod contracts, and separated persistent state from derived presentation. At CModel he worked across the migration to a Supabase/TypeScript stack, and at MusicBreakr he mapped heterogeneous external data onto internal creator, promotion, and campaign models and designed access patterns that held up as ingestion volume grew.

themes.title: Integrate external APIs into the product
themes.narrative: This is his strongest area. He has implemented and maintained production integrations with Microsoft 365/Graph, SharePoint, Teams, DocuSign, HubSpot, Monday, Harvest, Freshdesk, and Google services, including OAuth flows, token lifecycle, pagination, and mapping third-party state into application models. At MusicBreakr he built rate-limit-aware ingestion across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Twitter/X, plus Stripe Connect for marketplace onboarding, transactions, and payouts — evidence he can handle both the happy path and the failure modes at external boundaries.

themes.title: Investigate and resolve production failures
themes.narrative: Reg debugs across boundaries, which is where real production failures live. At MusicBreakr he resolved production failures spanning application state, backend workflows, payment systems, and third-party APIs while the marketplace served active customers, requiring changes that preserved existing behavior. At CModel he reasons about integration failures — expired authorization, unexpected external state, APIs diverging from documentation — across both systems involved rather than treating the API call in isolation.

themes.title: Familiarity with education products
themes.narrative: The honest gap: the evidence shows no prior work on education products specifically. That said, his track record of building consumer products around evolving user state — Reaccord's personalized daily interface over goals, actions, and reflection — plus a demonstrated ability to form rapid mental models in unfamiliar domains suggests the domain transfer is a learning curve, not a structural risk. It is the one area where the case rests on transfer rather than direct evidence.

interviewQuestions: Walk us through a feature you took from ambiguous customer need to production: what did you decide, what did you defer, and how did you know it worked for real users?
How would you approach modeling learning-product data — learners, content, progress, outcomes — in a relational database, and what would you validate at the application boundary?
Tell us about a production failure that spanned your app and a third-party system. How did you find the cause and ship the fix without breaking existing behavior?
